# az-tf-mlz-virtual-network-gateway

A Fortytwo managed landing zone (MLZ) module for a hub virtual network's gateway, in AzAPI: the VPN or
ExpressRoute gateway (`Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworkGateways`), its public IP addresses, and its
on-premises sites (`localNetworkGateways`) and connections (`connections`). Virtual WAN gateways are other
resource types, owned by `az-tf-mlz-connectivity-vwan`.

- **VPN** (`gateway_type = "Vpn"`, default): `VpnGw1AZ` (default) to `VpnGw5AZ`, the SKUs Azure still
  creates; the generation follows the SKU unless set. Active-standby or active-active (switched in place),
  BGP with custom APIPA addresses, and point-to-site with Microsoft Entra ID and/or certificates.
- **ExpressRoute** (`gateway_type = "ExpressRoute"`): `ErGw1AZ` to `ErGw3AZ`, or `ErGwScale` with its
  scale units. Azure assigns and manages its public IP address.
- **Public IP addresses** per IP configuration, created through
  [`az-tf-mlz-public-ip`](https://github.com/fortytwoservices/az-tf-mlz-public-ip) or given by ID. A
  created address that is removed (active-active to active-standby) is deleted only after the gateway has
  let go of it, in one apply.
- **Local network gateways and connections** through `modules/local_network_gateway` and
  `modules/connection`, which can also be called alone (for example from a state that holds a site's
  connections). Connections are `IPsec`, `Vnet2Vnet` or `ExpressRoute`; their keys are ephemeral and
  write-only (`connection_secrets`), sent again when `secret_version` changes. A replaced gateway
  replaces its connections, and so does a changed site (Azure does not move a connection).
- **Every setting is sent**, off or empty when unset, so removing one reaches Azure. BGP settings always
  carry one peering address entry per gateway instance, which keeps plans clean.
- **Replacement:** changing the type, the subnet, the generation or the first IP configuration (Azure
  does not change a gateway's first public IP address) replaces the gateway. A virtual network holds one
  VPN gateway, so the old one is deleted first.
- Lock, role assignments and diagnostic settings, as in Azure Verified Modules, through
  [`az-tf-mlz-interfaces`](https://github.com/fortytwoservices/az-tf-mlz-interfaces), on the gateway (its
  five log categories and metrics), each local network gateway (no diagnostic settings: Azure refuses
  them) and each connection (metrics only). A `ReadOnly` lock blocks updates of the locked resource
  itself; remove it before changing the gateway.
- Creating, changing or deleting a gateway takes up to 45 minutes, so `timeouts` default to 90 minutes.
  Azure sometimes fails a gateway write with `VmssGatewayDeploymentFailed` ("an intermittent error.
  Please try again"); `retry` cannot repeat a failed operation, so run the apply again.

```hcl
module "virtual_network_gateway" {
  source = "git::https://github.com/fortytwoservices/az-tf-mlz-virtual-network-gateway.git?ref=vX.Y.Z"

  name          = "vgw-hub-sdc"
  parent_id     = "/subscriptions/<subscription>/resourceGroups/<resource group>"
  location      = "swedencentral"
  subnet_id     = "<GatewaySubnet ID>"
  active_active = true
  bgp           = { asn = 65010 }
  ip_configurations = {
    ipconfig1 = { public_ip = { name = "pip-vgw-hub-sdc-1" } }
    ipconfig2 = { public_ip = { name = "pip-vgw-hub-sdc-2" } }
  }
  local_network_gateways = {
    oslo = { name = "lgw-oslo", gateway_ip_address = "<device IP>", address_prefixes = ["10.50.0.0/16"] }
  }
  connections = {
    oslo = { name = "con-oslo", local_network_gateway_key = "oslo" }
  }
  connection_secrets = { oslo = var.oslo_shared_key } # an ephemeral variable or an ephemeral resource's value
}
```

The examples deploy an active-active VPN gateway with BGP, point-to-site and one site (`default`), and an
ExpressRoute gateway (`express_route`).

## Required Inputs

The following input variables are required:

### <a name="input_location"></a> [location](#input\_location)

Description: Azure region of the gateway, and of the public IP addresses, local network gateways and connections the module creates, for example `swedencentral`.

Type: `string`

### <a name="input_name"></a> [name](#input\_name)

Description: Name of the virtual network gateway.

Type: `string`

### <a name="input_parent_id"></a> [parent\_id](#input\_parent\_id)

Description: Resource ID of the resource group the gateway and everything the module creates are created in. The gateway's IP configuration IDs are built from it, so pass it as Azure returns it (`/subscriptions/<id>/resourceGroups/<name>`).

Type: `string`

### <a name="input_subnet_id"></a> [subnet\_id](#input\_subnet\_id)

Description: Resource ID of the virtual network's `GatewaySubnet`: /27 or larger, /26 or larger for `ErGwScale` (Azure: `GatewaySubnetTooSmallForExpressrouteGatewaySku`; Microsoft Learn, "Configure a scalable ExpressRoute gateway"). The subnet belongs to the caller (the hub composition creates it); a VPN gateway and an ExpressRoute gateway can share it. Changing it replaces the gateway.

Type: `string`

## Optional Inputs

The following input variables are optional (have default values):

### <a name="input_active_active"></a> [active\_active](#input\_active\_active)

Description: VPN only: active-active, two gateway instances each with its own public IP address and tunnels, so `ip_configurations` holds two (three with `point_to_site`). Azure switches a gateway either way in place, in about 45 minutes; with BGP, the gateway's BGP peer addresses change (Microsoft Learn, "Change a VPN gateway mode: active-active").

Type: `bool`

Default: `false`

### <a name="input_bgp"></a> [bgp](#input\_bgp)

Description: (Optional) VPN only: BGP on the gateway. Null turns it off.

- `asn` - (Optional) The gateway's ASN. Defaults to `65515`, Azure's own, which on-premises peers cannot use. ASNs Azure or IANA reserve otherwise are refused (8074, 8075, 12076, 65517 to 65520, 23456, 64496 to 64511, 65535 to 65551); private ASNs are 64512 to 65514 and 65521 to 65534 (Microsoft Learn, VPN Gateway FAQ).
- `peer_weight` - (Optional) Weight added to routes learned from BGP peers, 0 to 100. Defaults to `0`.

Azure assigns the BGP peer addresses from `GatewaySubnet`, one per gateway instance (output `bgp_settings`); custom APIPA addresses are set per IP configuration (`ip_configurations.*.apipa_addresses`).

Type:

```hcl
object({
    asn         = optional(number, 65515)
    peer_weight = optional(number, 0)
  })
```

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_connection_secrets"></a> [connection\_secrets](#input\_connection\_secrets)

Description: The connections' keys, by `connections` key: the pre-shared key of an `IPsec` or `Vnet2Vnet` connection (required), the authorization key of an `ExpressRoute` connection to a circuit in another subscription (optional). Ephemeral and write-only: sent to Azure, never stored in state; change the connection's `secret_version` to send a new key.

Type: `map(string)`

Default: `{}`

### <a name="input_connections"></a> [connections](#input\_connections)

Description: Connections of the gateway, by a stable key, created through `modules/connection` (its README describes every field). Their keys go in `connection_secrets` under the same key. A replaced gateway keeps its resource ID, so its connections are replaced with it; a connection is also replaced when its site changes.

- `name` - Name of the connection.
- `type` - (Optional) `IPsec` (default), `Vnet2Vnet` or `ExpressRoute`.
- `local_network_gateway_key` or `local_network_gateway_id` - IPsec: a key of `local_network_gateways`, or an existing local network gateway's ID.
- `peer_virtual_network_gateway_id` - Vnet2Vnet: the other gateway's ID.
- `express_route_circuit_id` - ExpressRoute: the circuit's ID.
- `custom_bgp_addresses` - (Optional) IPsec: the custom APIPA BGP address to use, by IP configuration name of this gateway (one of that configuration's `apipa_addresses`).
- `enable_bgp`, `connection_protocol`, `connection_mode`, `dpd_timeout_seconds`, `routing_weight`, `use_policy_based_traffic_selectors`, `ipsec_policy`, `express_route_gateway_bypass`, `secret_version` - (Optional) As in `modules/connection`.
- `lock`, `role_assignments`, `diagnostic_settings` - (Optional) On the connection, as the module's own; diagnostic settings take `metrics` only (`AllMetrics`), a connection having no log categories.

### <a name="input_diagnostic_settings"></a> [diagnostic\_settings](#input\_diagnostic\_settings)

Description: A map of diagnostic settings to create on the resource. The map key is deliberately arbitrary to avoid issues where map keys maybe unknown at plan time.

- `name` - (Optional) The name of the diagnostic setting. One will be generated if not set, however this will not be unique if you want to create multiple diagnostic setting resources.
- `logs` - (Optional) A set of log entries to send to the destination. Each entry has the following attributes:
  - `category` - (Optional) The name of a specific log category to enable. Mutually exclusive with `category_group`.
  - `category_group` - (Optional) The name of a log category group to enable (for example, `allLogs` or `audit`). Mutually exclusive with `category`.
  - `enabled` - (Optional) Whether the log entry is enabled. Defaults to `true`.
  - `retention_policy` - (Optional) The retention policy for the log entry.
    - `days` - (Optional) The retention period in days. Defaults to `0` (retain indefinitely).
    - `enabled` - (Optional) Whether the retention policy is enabled. Defaults to `false`.
- `metrics` - (Optional) A set of metric entries to send to the destination. Each entry has the following attributes:
  - `category` - (Optional) The name of the metric category to enable.
  - `enabled` - (Optional) Whether the metric entry is enabled. Defaults to `true`.
  - `retention_policy` - (Optional) The retention policy for the metric entry, with the same `days` and `enabled` attributes as `logs.retention_policy`.
- `log_analytics_destination_type` - (Optional) The destination type for the diagnostic setting. Possible values are `Dedicated` and `AzureDiagnostics`. Defaults to `Dedicated`.
- `workspace_resource_id` - (Optional) The resource ID of the log analytics workspace to send logs and metrics to.
- `storage_account_resource_id` - (Optional) The resource ID of the storage account to send logs and metrics to.
- `event_hub_authorization_rule_resource_id` - (Optional) The resource ID of the event hub authorization rule to send logs and metrics to.
- `event_hub_name` - (Optional) The name of the event hub. If none is specified, the default event hub will be selected.
- `marketplace_partner_resource_id` - (Optional) The full ARM resource ID of the Marketplace resource to which you would like to send Diagnostic Logs.

Type:

```hcl
      }), {})

    metrics = optional(set(object({
```

### <a name="input_ignore_body_changes"></a> [ignore\_body\_changes](#input\_ignore\_body\_changes)

Description: Paths in each resource's `body` whose changes the AzAPI provider ignores. Prefer Terraform's `lifecycle.ignore_changes` when the paths are static; use this variable when the paths must be derived from variables or other non-static values.

Paths use dot notation, for example `properties.vpnClientConfiguration`. Individual list items cannot be targeted; ignore the whole list property instead. Configuration changes at an ignored path are **not** sent to Azure until that path is removed from the list. Changes take effect only after an apply, because the value is held in provider-private state.

- `network_virtual_network_gateways` - Ignored body paths for the gateway.
- `authorization_locks` - Ignored body paths for the gateway's lock.
- `authorization_role_assignments` - Ignored body paths for the gateway's role assignments.
- `insights_diagnostic_settings` - Ignored body paths for the gateway's diagnostic settings.
- `network_public_ip_addresses` - Slot for the `az-tf-mlz-public-ip` calls (its `network_public_ip_addresses` and interface keys).
- `network_local_network_gateways` - Slot for `modules/local_network_gateway` (its `network_local_network_gateways` and interface keys).
- `network_connections` - Slot for `modules/connection` (its `network_connections` and interface keys).

Type:

```hcl
    authorization_locks              = optional(list(string), [])
    authorization_role_assignments   = optional(list(string), [])

    network_public_ip_addresses = optional(object({
```

### <a name="input_ip_configurations"></a> [ip\_configurations](#input\_ip\_configurations)

Description: VPN only, and required for it: the gateway's IP configurations, by name, in name order. The first holds instance 0, the second instance 1 of an active-active gateway; one for active-standby, two for active-active, and a third, for point-to-site, when an active-active gateway has `point_to_site`. An ExpressRoute gateway takes none: Azure assigns and manages its public IP address, and the module names its one IP configuration `default`.

- `public_ip` - (Optional) A public IP address the module creates through `az-tf-mlz-public-ip` (Standard, static, its zones left to Azure: zone-redundant where the region has zones): `name`, and optionally `public_ip_prefix_id`.
- `public_ip_resource_id` - (Optional) An existing Standard public IP address with static allocation instead. Exactly one of the two.
- `apipa_addresses` - (Optional) Custom APIPA BGP addresses of this instance, from 169.254.21.0 to 169.254.22.255, for on-premises devices that peer over APIPA addresses. Needs `bgp`; not on the point-to-site IP configuration.

Azure does not change a gateway's first public IP address (Microsoft Learn, "Manage a public IP address with a VPN gateway"), so changing the first IP configuration's name or address replaces the gateway; keep its name first in order. Adding and removing the others (active-standby to active-active and back) updates the gateway in place, and a created address that is removed is deleted only after the gateway has let go of it.

Type:

```hcl
map(object({
    public_ip = optional(object({
      name                = string
      public_ip_prefix_id = optional(string)
    }))
    public_ip_resource_id = optional(string)
    apipa_addresses       = optional(list(string), [])
  }))
```

Default: `{}`

### <a name="input_local_network_gateways"></a> [local\_network\_gateways](#input\_local\_network\_gateways)

Description: On-premises sites, by a stable key, created through `modules/local_network_gateway` (its README describes every field); `connections` refer to them by key. Azure does not move a connection to another site, so a renamed site replaces its connections.

- `name` - Name of the local network gateway.
- `gateway_ip_address` or `fqdn` - The on-premises VPN device's public IP address or FQDN, exactly one.
- `address_prefixes` - (Optional) On-premises address ranges; may be empty with `bgp`, not without.
- `bgp` - (Optional) The device's `asn`, `bgp_peering_address` and `peer_weight`.
- `lock`, `role_assignments` - (Optional) On the local network gateway, as the module's own `lock` and `role_assignments`.

Type:

```hcl
map(object({
    name               = string
```

### <a name="input_lock"></a> [lock](#input\_lock)

Description: Controls the Resource Lock configuration for this resource. The following properties can be specified:

- `kind` - (Required) The type of lock. Possible values are `\"CanNotDelete\"` and `\"ReadOnly\"`.
- `name` - (Optional) The name of the lock. If not specified, a name will be generated based on the `kind` value. Changing this forces the creation of a new resource.
- `notes` - (Optional) Notes about the lock. This value maps to `Microsoft.Authorization/locks.properties.notes`.

Type:

```hcl
object({
    kind  = string
    name  = optional(string, null)
    notes = optional(string, null)
  })
```

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_point_to_site"></a> [point\_to\_site](#input\_point\_to\_site)

Description: (Optional) VPN only: point-to-site (user VPN). Null turns it off.

- `address_space` - Address ranges the VPN clients get addresses from, in CIDR notation; they must not overlap the virtual network or on-premises ranges.
- `protocols` - (Optional) `OpenVPN`, `IkeV2` and/or `SSTP`, but not `OpenVPN` with `SSTP` (Microsoft Learn: they "can't be enabled together"). Defaults to `["OpenVPN"]`.
- `entra_id` - (Optional) Microsoft Entra ID authentication in Azure's public cloud (OpenVPN only, with the Azure VPN Client): `tenant_id`, and `audience`, which defaults to the Microsoft-registered Azure VPN Client (`c632b3df-fb67-4d84-bdcf-b95ad541b5c8`; Microsoft Learn, "Configure P2S VPN Gateway for Microsoft Entra ID authentication").
- `root_certificates` - (Optional) Certificate authentication: trusted root certificates, by name, as their Base64 public data (without the BEGIN and END lines).
- `revoked_certificates` - (Optional) Revoked client certificates, by name, as their thumbprints.

At least one of `entra_id` and `root_certificates`. An active-active gateway needs a third IP configuration for point-to-site.

Type:

```hcl
object({
    address_space = list(string)
    protocols     = optional(list(string), ["OpenVPN"])
    entra_id = optional(object({
      tenant_id = string
      audience  = optional(string, "c632b3df-fb67-4d84-bdcf-b95ad541b5c8")
    }))
    root_certificates    = optional(map(string), {})
    revoked_certificates = optional(map(string), {})
  })
```

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_retry"></a> [retry](#input\_retry)

Description: Retry configuration applied to every `azapi` resource managed by the module and the modules it calls. Defaults retry `AnotherOperationInProgress`, which Azure returns while another operation runs on the same gateway or virtual network; any field can be overridden.

- `error_message_regex`  - (Optional) A list of regex patterns matching error messages that trigger a retry. Defaults to `["AnotherOperationInProgress"]`.
- `interval_seconds`     - (Optional) Initial interval between retries in seconds. Defaults to `30`.
- `max_interval_seconds` - (Optional) Maximum interval between retries in seconds. Defaults to `300`.

See <https://registry.terraform.io/providers/Azure/azapi/latest/docs/resources/resource#retry> for full semantics.

Type:

```hcl
object({
    error_message_regex  = optional(list(string), ["AnotherOperationInProgress"])
    interval_seconds     = optional(number, 30)
    max_interval_seconds = optional(number, 300)
  })
```

Default: `{}`

### <a name="input_role_assignments"></a> [role\_assignments](#input\_role\_assignments)

Description: A map of role assignments to create on the gateway. The map key is deliberately arbitrary to avoid issues where map keys maybe unknown at plan time.

- `name` - (Optional) The name of the role assignment. If not set, a random UUID will be generated. Changing this forces the creation of a new resource.
- `role_definition_id_or_name` - The ID or name of the role definition to assign to the principal.
- `principal_id` - The ID of the principal to assign the role to.
- `description` - (Optional) The description of the role assignment.
- `skip_service_principal_aad_check` - (Optional) If set to true, skips the Azure Active Directory check for the service principal in the tenant. Defaults to false.
- `condition` - (Optional) The condition which will be used to scope the role assignment.
- `condition_version` - (Optional) The version of the condition syntax. Leave as `null` if you are not using a condition, if you are then valid values are '2.0'.
- `delegated_managed_identity_resource_id` - (Optional) The delegated Azure Resource Id which contains a Managed Identity. Changing this forces a new resource to be created. This field is only used in cross-tenant scenario.
- `principal_type` - (Optional) The type of the `principal_id`. Possible values are `User`, `Group` and `ServicePrincipal`. It is necessary to explicitly set this attribute when creating role assignments if the principal creating the assignment is constrained by ABAC rules that filters on the PrincipalType attribute.

> Note: only set `skip_service_principal_aad_check` to true if you are assigning a role to a service principal.

Type:

```hcl
map(object({
    name                                   = optional(string, null)
    role_definition_id_or_name             = string
    principal_id                           = string
    description                            = optional(string, null)
    skip_service_principal_aad_check       = optional(bool, false)
    condition                              = optional(string, null)
    condition_version                      = optional(string, null)
    delegated_managed_identity_resource_id = optional(string, null)
    principal_type                         = optional(string, null)
  }))
```

Default: `{}`

### <a name="input_sku"></a> [sku](#input\_sku)

Description: Gateway SKU. VPN: `VpnGw1AZ` to `VpnGw5AZ` (Microsoft Learn, "VPN Gateway SKU consolidation and migration": no new non-AZ gateways since 2025-11-01; `Basic` lacks BGP and active-active and is not for production). ExpressRoute: `ErGw1AZ`, `ErGw2AZ`, `ErGw3AZ` or `ErGwScale` (with `express_route_scale_units`, in a `GatewaySubnet` of /26 or larger). Azure resizes a gateway in place within its family and generation; it does not downgrade an ExpressRoute gateway.

Type: `string`

Default: `"VpnGw1AZ"`

### <a name="input_tags"></a> [tags](#input\_tags)

Description: (Optional) Tags of the gateway, and of the public IP addresses, local network gateways and connections the module creates.

Type: `map(string)`

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_timeouts"></a> [timeouts](#input\_timeouts)

Description: Per-operation timeouts applied to every `azapi` resource managed by the module and the modules it calls. Creating, changing or deleting a gateway takes up to 45 minutes (Microsoft Learn), more than the provider's 30-minute default, so create, update and delete default to `90m`; any field can be overridden. Each value is a Go duration string (e.g. `30m`, `1h`).

- `create` - (Optional) Timeout for create operations. Defaults to `90m`.
- `read`   - (Optional) Timeout for read operations. Defaults to the provider's.
- `update` - (Optional) Timeout for update operations. Defaults to `90m`.
- `delete` - (Optional) Timeout for delete operations. Defaults to `90m`.

Type:

```hcl
object({
    create = optional(string, "90m")
    read   = optional(string)
    update = optional(string, "90m")
    delete = optional(string, "90m")
  })
```

Default: `{}`

### <a name="input_vpn_generation"></a> [vpn\_generation](#input\_vpn\_generation)

Description: (Optional) VPN only: `Generation1` or `Generation2`. Defaults to the SKU's: `Generation1` for `VpnGw1AZ` (it has no other), `Generation2` for the others (`VpnGw2AZ` and `VpnGw3AZ` come in both; Microsoft Learn, "About gateway SKUs"). Changing it replaces the gateway, so set `Generation1` to resize a `VpnGw1AZ` gateway in place to `VpnGw2AZ` or `VpnGw3AZ`.

Type: `string`

Default: `null`

## Outputs

The following outputs are exported:

### <a name="output_bgp_settings"></a> [bgp\_settings](#output\_bgp\_settings)

Description: The gateway's BGP settings as Azure reports them, for the on-premises side; null if Azure reports none.

- `asn` - The gateway's ASN.
- `peering_addresses` - By IP configuration name: `default` (the addresses Azure assigns from `GatewaySubnet`), `custom` (the APIPA addresses set) and `tunnel` (the instance's public IP addresses).

### <a name="output_connection_resource_ids"></a> [connection\_resource\_ids](#output\_connection\_resource\_ids)

Description: Resource IDs of the connections, by `connections` key.

### <a name="output_ip_configuration_ids"></a> [ip\_configuration\_ids](#output\_ip\_configuration\_ids)

Description: Resource IDs of the gateway's IP configurations, by name: for a connection's custom BGP addresses set outside this module.

### <a name="output_local_network_gateway_resource_ids"></a> [local\_network\_gateway\_resource\_ids](#output\_local\_network\_gateway\_resource\_ids)

Description: Resource IDs of the local network gateways, by `local_network_gateways` key.

### <a name="output_name"></a> [name](#output\_name)

Description: Name of the virtual network gateway.

### <a name="output_public_ip_address_ids"></a> [public\_ip\_address\_ids](#output\_public\_ip\_address\_ids)

Description: Resource IDs of the gateway's public IP addresses, created or given, by IP configuration name; empty for an ExpressRoute gateway, whose address Azure manages.

### <a name="output_public_ip_addresses"></a> [public\_ip\_addresses](#output\_public\_ip\_addresses)

Description: IP addresses of the public IP addresses the module creates, by IP configuration name.

### <a name="output_resource_id"></a> [resource\_id](#output\_resource\_id)

Description: Resource ID of the virtual network gateway.

## Development

Tools: Terraform 1.17.0, TFLint 0.65.0, terraform-docs 0.24.0 (the versions CI uses).

| What | Command |
|---|---|
| Format, validate, lint, unit tests, README drift (what CI runs) | `scripts/check.sh` |
| Format the code and regenerate the READMEs first | `scripts/check.sh --fix` |
| Integration tests in Azure | `ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID=<test subscription> scripts/integration.sh [dir ...]` |
| Examples: apply, plan again (must be empty), destroy | `ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID=<test subscription> scripts/e2e.sh [examples/<name> ...]` |

`README.md` files are generated from `_header.md`, the code and `_footer.md`; do not edit them by hand.

## Versions and releases

Every release is a SemVer tag `vX.Y.Z`; tags never move, and `main` is never consumed. Pin a release:

```hcl
source = "git::https://github.com/fortytwoservices/<repository>.git?ref=vX.Y.Z"
```

Pull requests are squash-merged, and their titles follow Conventional Commits, which set the next
version: `fix:` a patch, `feat:` a minor (a patch before 1.0.0), `feat!:` or `fix!:` a major (a minor
before 1.0.0). `docs:`, `test:`, `ci:`, `chore:` and `refactor:` release nothing. release-please keeps a
release pull request open; merging it writes `CHANGELOG.md`, the tag and the GitHub release.
